checks: exact HTTPS resident recipe starts independently and rejects unmatched routes, origins and missing admission credentials
an admitted HTTPS caller with an ungranted signing key receives no authenticated application history
a cold native client completes one direct HTTPS offer and authenticates through the actual resident context
the authenticated RTC channel retains original native signed records without more HTTPS introduction work
resident task abort closes the HTTPS listener and authenticated peer lifetime without retained entries or abort listeners
synchronous abort before listening and bind failure both dispose the handler and external abort listeners

metrics.byteBoundary: Logical peer frame payload bytes exclude RTC headers, credits and IP/UDP/DTLS/SCTP overhead.
metrics.network: Both native RTC peers use loopback UDP. HTTPS verifies the generated loopback certificate; no TLS checks are disabled.

qualification: Actual native HTTPS resident task, admission and reader-grant refusal, one authorized cold RTC connection, original signed records and unchanged introduction counters during application work, then verified abort and startup cleanup.
limits: This focused check validates reported observations and exact recipe identity; the workflow supplies runtime execution evidence.
The failed native session is the intentional admitted-but-ungranted signing-key rejection.
Native/native loopback evidence does not establish browser Worker transfer, deployed certificates, public NAT, TURN or provider billing.
